q-98325.name: Question 1
q-98325.problem:
Suppose that $f(x,y)$ is a differentiable function such that

$$
f(1,3)=4,\,{f}_{x}(1,3)=2,\,{f}_{y}(1,3)=1.
$$

Using a linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(1,3),$ estimate the value of $f(1.02,3.02).$
q-98325.worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y)≈f(a,b)+∇f(a,b)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(1,3)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ≈f(1,3)+∇f(1,3)\cdot ⟨x-1,y-3⟩ \\  & =f(1,3)+⟨{f}_{x}(1,3),{f}_{y}(1,3)⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,y-3⟩ \\  & =4+⟨2,1⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,y-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $f(1.02,3.02)$ by evaluating the linear approximation at $x=1.02$ and $y=3.02,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1.02,3.02) & ≈4+⟨2,1⟩\cdot ⟨1.02-1,3.02-3⟩ \\  & =4+⟨2,1⟩\cdot ⟨0.02,0.02⟩ \\  & =4+0.04+0.02 \\  & =4.06\end{aligned}
$$

So, the linear approximation of f at the point (1,3) is f(x,y)≈f(1,3)+∇f(1,3)⋅⟨x−1,y−3⟩=f(1,3)+⟨fx(1,3),fy(1,3)⟩⋅⟨x−1,y−3⟩=4+⟨2,1⟩⋅⟨x−1,y−3⟩.

q-98332.name: Question 2
q-98332.problem:
Let $f(x,y)$ be a differentiable function such that

$$
f(-1,1)=3,\,{f}_{x}(x,y)=4x,\,{f}_{y}(x,y)=2y.
$$

Using a linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(-1,1),$ estimate the value of $f(-0.95,0.95).$
q-98332.worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y)≈f(a,b)+∇f(a,b)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(-1,1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ≈f(-1,1)+∇f(-1,1)\cdot ⟨x+1,y-1⟩ \\  & =f(-1,1)+⟨{f}_{x}(-1,1),{f}_{y}(-1,1)⟩\cdot ⟨x+1,y-1⟩ \\  & =3+⟨{f}_{x}(-1,1),{f}_{y}(-1,1)⟩\cdot ⟨x+1,y-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${f}_{x}(-1,1)$ and ${f}_{y}(-1,1)$ using the given partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(-1,1) & =4(-1)=-4 \\ {f}_{y}(-1,1) & =2(1)=2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
f(x,y)≈3+⟨-4,2⟩\cdot ⟨x+1,y-1⟩.
$$

Finally, we can estimate $f(-0.95,0.95)$ by evaluating the linear approximation at $x=-0.95$ and $y=0.95,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-0.95,0.95) & ≈3+⟨-4,2⟩\cdot ⟨-0.95+1,0.95-1⟩ \\  & =3+⟨-4,2⟩\cdot ⟨0.05,-0.05⟩ \\  & =3-0.2-0.1 \\  & =2.7\end{aligned}
$$

q-98340.name: Question 3
q-98340.problem:
Suppose that $f(x,y,z)$ is a differentiable function such that

$$
f(1,-1,2)=6,\,{f}_{x}(1,-1,2)=-4,\,{f}_{y}(1,-1,2)=-1,\,{f}_{z}(1,-1,2)=3.
$$

Using a linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(1,-1,2)$ estimate the value of $f(1.04,-0.99,2.02).$
q-98340.worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b,c)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y,z)≈f(a,b,c)+∇f(a,b,c)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b,z-c⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(1,-1,2)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & ≈f(1,-1,2)+∇f(1,-1,2)\cdot ⟨x-1,y+1,z-2⟩ \\  & =f(1,-1,2)+⟨{f}_{x}(1,-1,2),{f}_{y}(1,-1,2),{f}_{z}(1,-1,2)⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,y+1,z-2⟩ \\  & =6+⟨-4,-1,3⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,y+1,z-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $f(1.04,-0.99,2.02)$ by evaluating the linear approximation at $x=1.04,$ $y=-0.99,$ and $z=2.02$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1.04,-0.99,2.02) & ≈6+⟨-4,-1,3⟩\cdot ⟨1.04-1,-0.99+1,2.02-2⟩ \\  & =6+⟨-4,-1,3⟩\cdot ⟨0.04,0.01,0.02⟩ \\  & =6-0.16-0.01+0.06 \\  & =5.89\end{aligned}
$$

q-129631.name: Question 4
q-129631.problem:
Suppose that $f(x,y)$ is a differentiable function such that

$$
f(2,0)=0,\,{f}_{x}(2,0)=0,\,{f}_{y}(2,0)=2.
$$

Using a linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(2,0),$ estimate the value of $f(2.01,0.02).$
q-129631.worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y)≈f(a,b)+∇f(a,b)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(2,0)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ≈f(2,0)+∇f(2,0)\cdot ⟨x-2,y-0⟩ \\  & =f(2,0)+⟨{f}_{x}(2,0),{f}_{y}(2,0)⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,y⟩ \\  & =0+⟨0,2⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,y⟩ \\  & =⟨0,2⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,y⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $f(2.01,0.02)$ by evaluating the linear approximation at $x=2.01$ and $y=0.02,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2.01,0.02) & ≈⟨0,2⟩\cdot ⟨2.01-2,0.02⟩ \\  & =⟨0,2⟩\cdot ⟨0.01,0.02⟩ \\  & =0(0.01)+2(0.02) \\  & =0+0.04 \\  & =0.04\end{aligned}
$$

q-129631.html:
Question 4
?

Suppose that f(x,y) is a differentiable function such that f(2,0)=0,fx(2,0)=0,fy(2,0)=2.

Using a linear approximation of f at the point (2,0), estimate the value of f(2.01,0.02).

a
0.08
b
0.13
c
0.04
d
0.01
e
0.11
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The linear approximation of the function f at the point (a,b) is given by f(x,y)≈f(a,b)+∇f(a,b)⋅⟨x−a,y−b⟩.

So, the linear approximation of f at the point (2,0) is f(x,y)≈f(2,0)+∇f(2,0)⋅⟨x−2,y−0⟩=f(2,0)+⟨fx(2,0),fy(2,0)⟩⋅⟨x−2,y⟩=0+⟨0,2⟩⋅⟨x−2,y⟩=⟨0,2⟩⋅⟨x−2,y⟩.

We can approximate f(2.01,0.02) by evaluating the linear approximation at x=2.01 and y=0.02, as follows: f(2.01,0.02)≈⟨0,2⟩⋅⟨2.01−2,0.02⟩=⟨0,2⟩⋅⟨0.01,0.02⟩=0(0.01)+2(0.02)=0+0.04=0.04

q-129634.name: Question 5
q-129634.problem:
Suppose that $f(x,y)$ is a differentiable function such that

$$
f(1,-1)=-2,\,{f}_{x}(1,-1)=1,\,{f}_{y}(1,-1)=6.
$$

Using a linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(1,-1),$ estimate the value of $f(0.96,-0.95).$
q-129634.worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y)≈f(a,b)+∇f(a,b)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(1,-1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ≈f(1,-1)+∇f(1,-1)\cdot ⟨x-1,y-(-1)⟩ \\  & =f(1,-1)+⟨{f}_{x}(1,-1),{f}_{y}(1,-1)⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,y+1⟩ \\  & =-2+⟨1,6⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,y+1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $f(0.96,-0.95)$ by evaluating the linear approximation at $x=0.96$ and $y=-0.95,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0.96,-0.95) & ≈-2+⟨1,6⟩\cdot ⟨0.96-1,-0.95+1⟩ \\  & =-2+⟨1,6⟩\cdot ⟨-0.04,0.05⟩ \\  & =-2+1(-0.04)+6(0.05) \\  & =-2-0.04+0.3 \\  & =-1.74\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Suppose that f(x,y) is a differentiable function such that f(1,−1)=−2,fx(1,−1)=1,fy(1,−1)=6. Using a linear approximation of f at the point (1,−1), estimate the value of f(0.96,−0.95).

a
−1.97
b
−1.74
c
−1.85
d
−2.04
e
−2.11
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The linear approximation of the function f at the point (a,b) is given by f(x,y)≈f(a,b)+∇f(a,b)⋅⟨x−a,y−b⟩.

So, the linear approximation of f at the point (1,−1) is f(x,y)≈f(1,−1)+∇f(1,−1)⋅⟨x−1,y−(−1)⟩=f(1,−1)+⟨fx(1,−1),fy(1,−1)⟩⋅⟨x−1,y+1⟩=−2+⟨1,6⟩⋅⟨x−1,y+1⟩

We can approximate f(0.96,−0.95) by evaluating the linear approximation at x=0.96 and y=−0.95, as follows: f(0.96,−0.95)≈−2+⟨1,6⟩⋅⟨0.96−1,−0.95+1⟩=−2+⟨1,6⟩⋅⟨−0.04,0.05⟩=−2+1(−0.04)+6(0.05)=−2−0.04+0.3=−1.74
